severity_scale.major: changes how a central result should be stated or read
severity_scale.moderate: changes a secondary claim, a denominator or what the reader can infer

locations.passage: The liquidation prompt gives the amount owed, the shortfall, the two lists and the player's holdings.

findings.finding: No draft quotes or describes the scenario note carried by every liquidation prompt, which tells the agent the menu will be refreshed and when to declare bankruptcy.
findings.evidence: All 439 stored LIQUIDATION_DECISION prompts carry the identical note: "Choose exactly one liquidation action now. The engine will apply it, update your cash/assets, and ask you again if you still cannot pay. Declare bankruptcy only when you cannot or should not raise enough cash." (fresh_checks.json: liquidation_scenario_notes; exact match at G20 d327 in quote_checks.json).
findings.recommendation: Quote the note in the methods. In the quit-or-continue result, say that declaring on an unpayable debt follows this instruction and that declaring on a payable debt follows the agent's own stated belief that it cannot pay. Keep the release rule and values out of the claim about what the note supplies; it states neither.

locations.passage: The table does show discrimination at the first menu. The agents quit almost always when no payment existed and almost never when one did.
Agents almost always quit when no payment existed and continued when one did.

findings.finding: The 50/56 against 3/131 comparison reproduces, but its payable denominator is dominated by 115 debts that cash, listed mortgages and listed building sales cover, which do not test whether an agent can see a route the menu hides. One of the three payable declarations is a channel conflict.
findings.evidence: Fresh: 50/56 above-bound and 3/131 payable debts declared at the first decision. Within the 72 debts whose visible sum (cash + listed mortgages + all salvage) falls short: 50/56 unpayable against 2/16 tier N. Above-bound debts with shortfall no larger than the largest tier N shortfall ($326): 15/19 declared; with debt/visible ratio no larger than 1.81: 20/24. Tiers A and B: 1/115 declared (G12 Grok d249, whose note and content describe a sale). Continuers: five Grok, one Gemini; Opus and Sol declared at once in all 27 of theirs.
findings.recommendation: Present the comparison inside the 72 visible-shortfall debts, with the matched-shortfall row, and name G12 Grok as a channel conflict. Call it agreement between the first choice and payability at population level, not sensitivity or calibrated difficulty, and state that the split was computed after the corpus was studied.

findings.evidence: Fresh: 18 of the 21 accepted non-completing swap or cash-bid openings answered Grok-authored offers. Without Grok-authored openings: 3/165 against 3/114. All forms: 32/524 openings accepted, 21 Grok-authored; Sol, Gemini and Opus openings 11/389; later offers 81/394. locations.passage: The response follows the event of completion and the form of the offer. It does not follow the measured size of what the rival could do next, which level four would require.
For rivals, stated concern and matching refusals attach to the event of completion, with no measured response to the size of the rival's opportunity.
their refusals tracked the event of completion and the form of the offer. They did not track the amount of building the rival could afford
The cells are small and cash omits mortgage capacity, but these slices give no sign that refusals scale with the rival's building power.

findings.finding: A flat rejection rate near a ceiling, on a coarse capacity measure, is read as evidence that refusals ignore the size of the rival's opportunity and respond to the event of completion.
findings.evidence: Fresh: completing swaps rejected 4/8, 26/33, 42/48, 23/27 by proposer house capacity (none, 1-2, 3-5, 6+); cash bids 2/3, 13/19, 7/20, 20/28; swaps by proposer post-trade cash terciles 29/38, 35/39, 31/39. Swap rejection is 79-88% in every bin with data. House counts treat a light-blue house and a dark-blue house alike (46 and 37 of the groups opening offers would complete) and ignore mortgage capacity.
findings.recommendation: Write: rejection of completing swaps is 79 to 88 percent in every capacity bin with data; this coarse measure shows no gradient, which neither supports nor excludes sensitivity to the size of the rival's opportunity. Drop 'follows/attaches to the event of completion' and 'does not follow the size'.

locations.passage: Since the prompt supplies none of these values, each one is a board fact the system recalled.
Payment had to use deeds that the first menu did not offer and that no prompt mentions as a resource.

findings.finding: Correct that no prompt states a mortgage value or the release rule; overstated in implying nothing in the prompt could carry them: the prompt carries the agent's own last ten notes, which sometimes carry values and, twice, the release rule. Purchase prompts also show a landed deed's price, from which a mortgage value can be derived.
findings.evidence: Fresh, sixteen first-decision prompts: no price, rent, mortgage-value, house-cost or group field (0/16); system prompt never mentions mortgages (0/16); 12/16 carry own notes; 11 of those state some mortgage or liquidity amount (e.g. G20 Sol "$325 idle mortgage capacity"); G1 Grok's carried note states the rule ("yellows cannot be mortgaged while it stands"); G18 Gemini's states it about an opponent; G4 Opus and G13 Gemini carry redemption costs of a to-be-released deed ($121, $193); by search and reading, none states a released deed's mortgage value.
findings.recommendation: Write: no prompt states a mortgage value or the release rule, and liquidation prompts show no prices; no carried note states the mortgage value of a deed the sales would release; listed capacity, and twice the rule, were carried in the agents' own notes. Report the carried-note observation under the memory question.

locations.passage: The whole-block resampling range is 24.2--35.5 points, but removing Grok authors changes it to $-3.8$--31.9.
The central 95\% resampling bands describe sensitivity to reweighting these five observed blocks.

findings.finding: Whole-block resampling is the only interval shown. With five blocks it has 126 distinct multisets and ignores variation among games within a block, so it is narrow by construction.
findings.evidence: Fresh: block-only 24.2 to 35.5 (all swaps) against two-stage 12.7 to 48.7 and games-only 13.8 to 48.2. Without Grok authors, block-only cash-bid band is -21.3 to -0.1 (excludes zero) against two-stage -32.9 to +8.7.
findings.recommendation: Show per-block values and leave-one-block-out ranges first, then the two-stage (blocks, then games within blocks) interval as the single summary; if block-only appears, state why it is narrow.

locations.passage: What differs is the kind of reply.

findings.finding: Counter rates and refusal wording are reported without non-completing baselines, which changes their reading.
findings.evidence: Fresh: counters 26/70 completing cash bids, 20/116 completing swaps, but also 32/103 and 18/72 in non-completing cells. Reciprocity wording in Gemini rejections: 28/62 completing against 1/59 non-completing. Commitment wording in Grok rejections: 38/54 against 12/36.
findings.recommendation: Print both cells. Say cash bids draw more counters than swaps in both cells and the gap widens under completion; Gemini's reciprocity rule is specific to completing offers; Grok's 'never' is partly a general refusal style.
